title: Agent output contracts
description: Structured results the engine requires from an agent turn. The prose an agent writes is its response and is stored verbatim as the step's response.md; these objects are the machine-readable part the engine acts on, and live in run metadata, not in the step.

fit.description: Is this playbook the right instrument for this issue?

issuePresent.description: Could the coordinator confirm the reported problem exists? false does not imply unfit — a strategy may still proceed to investigate.

handling.description: reworded: statement is now what one check run (drive) of a revision can prove, and original keeps the requested wording. operator-measurement: statement is kept; the measurement is listed for the operator at closure (residualRisks).

reason.description: Why the configured checks cannot produce the evidence as requested (repeated runs, a measurement on a live host, anything outside one drive per revision).

original.description: The requested wording, when handling is reworded.

outsideChecks.description: Present only on a criterion whose evidence, as requested, the run's configured checks cannot produce.

acceptanceCriteria.description: Recorded at triage and checked again at closure. Closure requires the coordinator to confirm these are satisfied.

suggestion.description: Recommended next action for the operator. Advisory only; does not archive the issue.

firstHandoff.description: Optional: the first worker assignment, written in the triage turn instead of a separate brief turn. The engine records it as that brief (validated the same way); omit it when the playbook does not fit or input is needed first.

windowDecision.description: The evidence window was just captured; the first assignment keeps it.

facts.description: Facts this triage established by reading the source snapshot or running a read-only command (Phase 1). Every fact the criteria or a needs-input decision rests on is listed with its evidence: a file and lines, or the command and what it printed.

autonomy.description: Can ONE run of this playbook finish the issue without asking anybody? autonomous: start the work. needs-owner-input: the run ends after triage and the issue owner is asked `questions` first. too-large: the run ends after triage and the owner is offered `split`. Technical choices, unknowns a worker can establish, and tools missing on this host are never a reason to ask.

questions.description: Only with needs-owner-input: what only the issue owner can decide, each answerable in a line.

category.description: owner-gate: the issue itself asks to stop for the owner's confirmation. requirement-conflict: criteria that cannot all hold, with evidence. authorization: spending, production, destroying data, publishing. missing-information: something only the owner knows (an account, a name, an intent) that no worker can find.

recommendation.description: What the agents would do, and why, so the owner can simply agree.

split.description: Only with too-large: the parts, each small enough for one run, in the order they should be done.

handoff.description: The coordinator authors the working prompt for another participant. The engine validates and delivers it; the coordinator never invokes anyone itself.

mustAddress.description: Finding ids this handoff is required to cover, when following a review.

windowDecision.description: Coordinator owns the evidence window. Refresh repeats this cycle with freshly captured logs; restart-required stops for new source snapshot.

operatorRequest.description: Last resort, rarely right. Work the run cannot do for itself because it belongs to the live checkout (most often a commit of the project's own checkout), an authorization only a person can give, a question a plan or an audit addresses to the owner on access, security or a documented promise, or a verified conflict between requirements that only the person who set them can settle. The engine pauses the run and asks one question. Never for a technical choice (decide it and record it under assumptions), for information a worker can establish, or for a tool missing on this host (use the configured staging infrastructure, or let the check be unavailable), or for a seat's permission to run something its approval layer refuses: no answer can change a seat's tools, and checks are rerun by the engine.

question.description: ONE question an operator can answer in one line. Not a list.

reason.description: Why the run cannot proceed without it, in terms of what was observed.

projectAction.description: The id of a project action that would do it, when the project offers one. It is a suggestion, not authority: whoever answers decides whether running it is warranted, and naming one the project does not offer only wastes the ask.

category.description: technical: a question about a technical route you cannot settle from the evidence you have (which layer to fix, whether an approach is sound, what an observed failure means). It goes to the consult panel, two senior models that read the code, and never to a person: their answer, or what each said when they differ, reaches you as a decision. Ask it instead of guessing an assumption you cannot judge. live-checkout: work only the live checkout can take. owner-gate: a stop the issue itself asks for at this point (for example after the plan; ask once, approve or revise, with the plan summarised in the owner's terms), or a question a plan or an audit addresses to the owner on access, security or a documented promise, which is never answered by you or recorded as an assumption. authorization: spending, production, destroying data, publishing. requirement-conflict: acceptance criteria that cannot all hold, shown with evidence.

recommendation.description: What you would do, so whoever answers can simply agree.

assumptions.description: Technical choices you made instead of asking, each with its reason. They are listed in the run's result for the owner to overrule afterwards.

resolves.description: Finding ids this revision claims to address.

diagnosticDrive.description: Only on the author turn that records a revision in a review loop: ask for one drive of the check target on this revision plus a patch kept outside the worktree. The variant is never the revision, never reviewed or delivered, and its result gates nothing.

reason.description: What this drive is meant to find out.

patch.description: A unified diff, as a path relative to your scratch directory.

tier.description: Which tier of a tiered target to drive; full when omitted.

basedOnRevision.description: The revision fingerprint this turn was told it starts from, echoed so a turn that worked from something else is detectable; null on the first implementation, when no candidate exists yet. The revision the turn PRODUCES is computed by the engine from the worktree after the turn and is never self-reported.

ownerHolds.description: Only when implementation must wait for the owner: a question on access, security or a documented promise that is neither your call nor the coordinator's. Never for a technical choice, which is decided and recorded as an assumption. The engine puts each hold to the owner before implementation goes on. A stated hold stands until the owner answers it, whatever a later output says or omits, so to change a question restate the same id. In a run with nothing to implement it stops nothing.

question.description: ONE question the owner can answer in one line.

category.description: What makes this the owner's: access a seat or a person has, a security trade-off, or something the documentation promises.

reason.description: Why this is the owner's decision in that category, in terms of what was observed.

recommendation.description: What you would do, so the owner can simply agree.

verdict.description: An auditor may only approve or request changes. 'blocked' is an engine state, never a verdict.

ownerHolds.description: Only when implementation must wait for the owner: a question on access, security or a documented promise that is neither your call nor the coordinator's. Never for a technical choice, which is decided and recorded as an assumption. The engine puts each hold to the owner before implementation goes on. A stated hold stands until the owner answers it, whatever a later output says or omits, so to change a question restate the same id. In a run with nothing to implement it stops nothing.

question.description: ONE question the owner can answer in one line.

category.description: What makes this the owner's: access a seat or a person has, a security trade-off, or something the documentation promises.

reason.description: Why this is the owner's decision in that category, in terms of what was observed.

recommendation.description: What you would do, so the owner can simply agree.

artifactRevision.description: The revision fingerprint this review examined. null when the artifact is not a code candidate — a plan review has nothing to fingerprint yet. A null revision can never satisfy sameRevisionApproval, so a plan approval cannot be mistaken for approval of code.

location.description: path:line where applicable. Required by the engine on every substantial finding (blocking, or major/critical).

criterion.description: What the finding violates: the acceptance criterion id, the plan commitment, or the invariant, quoted. Required by the engine on every substantial finding; a finding that cannot cite one is minor/info.

contradicts.description: Set only when this finding shows the artifact contradicts one of the brief's acceptance criteria: that criterion's id, exactly as the brief gives it. Such a finding is blocking whatever its severity, and the verdict must be changes-needed. Omit it for observations outside the criteria.

evidence.description: What was observed: the behaviour, the command run, the line read. Distinct from the description, which says what is wrong.

awaitsCheck.description: Set true only when the finding is blocking solely because a criterion needs evidence that the run's configured checks produce (for example the staging test drive) and that has no result for this revision yet, and nothing in the code is wrong. When every substantial finding of a round awaits the checks, the engine runs them on this revision once, even when they otherwise wait for approval, and the same reviewers review it again in the same round with the result. Never for a defect the author can fix.

failingTests.description: The exact names of the selftests this finding says fail, as a selftest report names them. Only where the run's checks declare a targeted tier does it change anything: a blocking finding's names are run on the author's next revision.

verification.description: What the reviewer actually did, so the depth of the audit is on record. gate: whether the project's own checks were executed by the reviewer (executed), deliberately not (not-executed, with notRun saying why), or could not be established (unknown).

performed.description: Commands run and files read, one per entry.

notRun.description: What was not verified and why.

priorFindings.description: Disposition of every plan-review finding the engine supplied in the context (findings.plan). Required whenever such findings exist: an implementation is not acceptable merely because its plan was, and a plan finding the implementation dropped must be named. `deferred` keeps the finding open and counts as substantial; `withdrawn` needs a reason.

reason.description: Where and how it was addressed, why it is deferred, or why it is withdrawn.

then.description: An approved review must carry no substantial findings, per the strategy's reviewPolicy. Enforced by the engine; contradiction triggers protocol repair.

unmet.description: Implementation and plan-and-implement runs: required when met is false, absent when it is true. Why the criterion is unmet. missing-work and missing-evidence return the run to the author (at most twice); the others stop it for the operator.

residualRisks.description: What remains unfixed, accepted as-is, or changed from the original acceptance criteria. Recorded on the run's closure so a closing report cannot silently treat every finding as repaired. Empty when nothing remains.

relatesTo.description: A finding or acceptance-criterion id, when one applies.

accepted.description: true when the coordinator judges the risk acceptable for closure; false when it must be tracked as follow-up.

windowDecision.description: Coordinator owns the evidence window. Refresh repeats this cycle with freshly captured logs; restart-required stops for new source snapshot.

documentArtifact.description: An author's document — analysis, specification, review, research — where the deliverable is the response itself and no candidate is fingerprinted.

resolves.description: Finding ids this revision claims to address.

openQuestions.description: Decisions only the operator can make, stated so closure can name them.

windowDecision.description: Coordinator owns the evidence window. Refresh repeats this cycle with freshly captured logs; restart-required stops for new source snapshot.
Assess the captured window. Request specific missing evidence through needs-information.

size.description: Order-of-magnitude sizing, not a design: minor (one write and one hand-over) or major (it needs a plan). The run records major whenever its seats disagree.

affectedModules.description: For a Boilerplate project, the affected modules as <collection>/<module> paths, framework and application modules alike; otherwise empty.

autonomy.description: Can ONE run of the recommended playbook finish the issue without asking anybody? autonomous: it may start (only an accepted report). needs-owner-input: the owner must answer `questions` first (also every disposition other than accepted, with the one question the owner must answer). too-large: the owner is offered `split`. Technical choices and unknowns a worker can establish are never a reason to ask.

questions.description: Only with needs-owner-input: what only the issue owner can decide, each answerable in a line.

category.description: owner-gate: the issue itself asks to stop for the owner's confirmation. requirement-conflict: criteria that cannot all hold, with evidence. authorization: spending, production, destroying data, publishing. missing-information: something only the owner knows (an account, a name, an intent) that no worker can find.

recommendation.description: What the agents would do, and why, so the owner can simply agree.

split.description: Only with too-large: the parts, each small enough for one run, in the order they should be done.

singleSeatResult.description: What a single, unreviewed seat returns: the author's artifact plus a structured outcome. completed says whether the task as asked is done; when it is not, blockers name what stopped it, so closure can refuse instead of resolving an unfinished task.

completed.description: true only when everything the task asked for is done and in the workspace. Partial work or work that needs a decision is false. Work that is done but that only the engine's own check after the turn can verify is true, with the open verification listed under unverified.

blockers.description: What stopped the task, one entry each. Required, non-empty, when completed is false.

unverified.description: Behaviour changed but not checked, one entry each.

basedOnRevision.description: The revision fingerprint this turn was told it starts from, echoed; null on the first implementation.
